title: MATH 3042 Statistics · Unit 5
subtitle: Continuous probability distributions: uniform, normal, exponential
description: Unit 5: why a continuous variable has P(X = x) = 0 and probabilities become areas; the probability density function and the cumulative function F(x); the uniform distribution on [a, b] and the bus-wait example; the normal distribution's shape and parameters, the standard normal Z table read forwards (areas) and backwards (percentiles), standardizing any normal X, the IQ, cosmic-radiation and Gaussian-noise bit-error examples; and the exponential distribution for waiting times, its cdf 1 - e^(-x/beta), mean = sd = beta, percentiles, and the memoryless property on the bank-teller example. Every example computed and checked with pnorm, qnorm, pexp, qexp. Ends with the examples worked, a mock quiz and a formula sheet.
intro:
:::quiz Quiz scope
The Unit 5 notes were posted blank and ahead of the lecture; every answer here is computed and labelled so, and the in-class numbers replace them if they differ. By the one-unit-behind pattern this unit's paper quiz will ask for: an area under a uniform density, a Z-table lookup in each direction (left tail, right tail, between, and a percentile), a normal problem that needs Z = (X - mu)/sigma first, and an exponential probability or percentile from F(x) = 1 - e^(-x/beta). Bring the Z table the course provides and a calculator with e^x and ln. The RStudio half will follow Lab 6, not yet posted.
:::

steps.note: take it cold first to find the gaps (about 35 min)
read P(Z <= -1.96), P(Z > 2.33), P(0.55 <= Z <= 1.10) off the table yourself
standardize first: IQ below 120, radiation 4.35 to 5.00, the 95th percentile at z = 1.645
the teller's conditional answer equals the unconditional one
the bus: (11 - 8)/20, (20 - 12)/20, and exactly 4 minutes is 0
every example with blank answer lines, worked; do them before reading
print it; rewrite the three distributions' rows from memory once
